problems.title: A rotated side passes through an original vertex
problems.question: An isosceles triangle with AB=BC=12 is rotated clockwise 30° about A. The original C lies on the rotated segment B₁C₁. Find area ABC.
problems.idea: Rotate C back by 30° to a point C′ on BC.
formulas: AC′=AC; angle CAC′=30°, so the base angles of isosceles triangle ACC′ are 75°.
steps: Because C′ lies on BC, angle ACB=75°.
The equal sides AB=BC give angle A=75°, so angle B=30°.
Area ABC=AB·BC·sin B/2=144·(1/2)/2.

problems.title: An apothem’s angle with a square-base diagonal
problems.question: A regular square pyramid’s apothem makes an angle with a base diagonal whose cosine is 1/√6. Find the angle between a lateral edge and the base plane.
problems.idea: Resolve the apothem into its horizontal and vertical components.
formulas: For base edge a and apothem l, the absolute component along a base diagonal is a/(2√2); a/(2√2l)=1/√6.
steps: Thus l=a√3/2. The height satisfies h²=l²−a²/4=a²/2.
The horizontal projection of a lateral edge is the circumradius a/√2, equal to h.
Therefore the edge’s inclination has tangent 1.

problems.title: Two diagonal sections of an oblique square prism
problems.question: A prism has square base of edge a. A₁C is perpendicular to the base and has length a. Section AA₁C₁C has area 4√2. Find section BB₁D₁D.
problems.idea: The horizontal component of a lateral edge is AC.
formulas: AC=a√2; height=a; lateral edge length L=√(2a²+a²)=a√3.
steps: Section AA₁C₁C has base AC and perpendicular height a, so its area is a²√2. Thus a²=4.
BD is perpendicular to AC and to the vertical direction, hence perpendicular to the lateral edge.
Section BB₁D₁D has area BD·L=a√2·a√3=a²√6.

problems.title: Join diagonal midpoints in a trapezoid
problems.question: In trapezoid ABCD, bases BC and AD satisfy AD:BC=4.5. Given AB=a and CD=b, express the vector from midpoint of AC to midpoint of BD.
steps: Group the numerator as (B−A)+(D−C)=AB+CD=a+b.
The base ratio is unnecessary for this vector expression.
problems.answer: (a+b)/2; reverse the sign for the opposite direction.

problems.title: The part of a union outside one event
problems.question: Independent A,B satisfy P(A∪B)=0.9 and P(A)=0.6. Find P(Aᶜ∩B).
problems.idea: The union is the disjoint sum of A and the part of B outside A.
steps: Subtract 0.6 from 0.9. Independence is not needed for this particular subtraction.

problems.title: Factor a sum of sine and cosine cubes
problems.question: Solve cos³x+sin³x=1−(1/2)sin2x.
problems.idea: Use the sum-of-cubes formula and sin2x=2sin x cos x.
formulas: cos³x+sin³x=(cos x+sin x)(1−sin x cos x).
steps: The equation becomes (1−sin x cos x)(cos x+sin x−1)=0.
The first factor is at least 1/2, so cos x+sin x=1.
Equivalently sin(x+π/4)=1/√2.

problems.title: A product inequality from sum-to-product
problems.question: Solve sin x sin3x>sin5x sin7x.
problems.idea: Convert both products into cosine differences.
steps: Thus sin8x sin4x<0. Since sin8x=2sin4x cos4x, this is 2sin²4x cos4x<0.
Require cos4x<0 and sin4x≠0.

problems.title: Equal binomial terms and zero factors
problems.question: The fifth and ninth terms in (2x+y)¹² are equal. Find x/y.
problems.idea: Use the symmetric binomial coefficients and keep zero-factor cases.
steps: For y≠0, equality reduces to x⁴[16x⁴−y⁴]=0 after cancellation of common nonzero constants and powers of y.
Thus x=0 or 2x=±y.
If both x and y are assumed nonzero, only the last two cases remain.
problems.answer: x/y=0,1/2,or −1/2 when the ratio is defined.
problems.note: The common textbook answer ±1/2 assumes x≠0. As printed, x=0,y≠0 also makes both named terms zero.

problems.title: Six-digit numbers with three even digits
problems.question: How many six-digit numbers have exactly three even and three odd digits?
problems.idea: Count all six-position strings, then remove those starting with zero.
formulas: There are 5 even digits including 0, and 5 odd digits.
steps: All strings with the required parity counts: C(6,3)·5⁶=312500.
Strings beginning with zero need 2 even and 3 odd digits in the remaining positions: C(5,2)·5⁵=31250.
Subtract to enforce the six-digit condition.

problems.title: A proposed identity that is false
problems.question: Prove the printed identity $\sqrt{1+\cos\alpha}+\sqrt{1-\sin\alpha}=2\sin(\alpha/2)$ for $0<\alpha<\pi/2$.
problems.idea: Test a permitted simple angle before attempting a proof.
steps: The left side is (√3+1+√2)/2, which exceeds 1.
The right side is 2sin15°=(√6−√2)/2, which is less than 1.
The two sides differ at an allowed angle, so the statement cannot be an identity.
problems.note: A sign, radicand or right-hand expression has been misprinted. The explanation gives a counterexample instead of proving a false claim.
